ball.motion.title: Projectile motion
captions: Gravity pulls the ball down all the time, so its path curves into a parabola.
Sideways speed never changes. Only the up-and-down speed does, because gravity acts down.
Air drag slows the ball, so the best angle drops below 45 degrees. Grey = no air.

ball.compare.title: Bounce
captions: Each bounce is lower because the ball keeps only part of its energy: the height ratio is e squared.
Falling turns height energy into movement; the squash stores it like a spring; some is lost as heat and sound every bounce.
Bounciness depends on the material: a super ball springs back almost fully, clay absorbs the energy as heat and barely bounces.

ball.flow.title: Follow the energy
captions: Your arm does work on the ball. A tennis ball thrown at 10 metres per second carries about 2.9 joules.
Going up, motion energy turns into height energy. At the top of a 45 degree throw it is half and half.
Coming down, height energy turns back into motion. A little is lost to air drag on the way.
On landing the motion energy becomes heat, sound and the next bounce. None of it is destroyed.

ball.number.title: The number
captions: Range is speed squared divided by g at 45 degrees: 100 divided by 9.81 is about 10 metres. Air is ignored.
The ball stays up for 1.4 seconds and peaks at 2.5 metres. Ten metres per second is 36 km/h.
The Moon pulls six times more weakly, so the same throw flies six times as far: about 62 metres.
